units.name: Directions and Maps
units.summary: North, south, east and west, and reading a simple map.

topics.name: Directions and Simple Maps
topics.summary: Using north, south, east and west to describe where things are.

objectives.text: Use the sun to work out which way is east and west.
Describe where something is on a simple map.

keyTerms.definition: The way you face or travel: north, south, east or west.
A drawing of a place, seen from above.
The part of a map that explains what each symbol means.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
There are four main directions.

You will learn their names and their order.

You will learn to find them using the sun.

You will learn to read a simple map.

sections.heading: The four directions
sections.body:
The four main directions are:

    NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, WEST

On a map they are drawn like this:

              N
              |
        W  ---+---  E
              |
              S

North is at the top. South at the bottom. East on the right. West on the left.

Going round clockwise from the top, the order is North, East, South, West.

Many people remember it with a sentence: Never Eat Slimy Worms. N, E, S, W.

sections.heading: Using the sun
sections.body:
You do not need anything to find the directions. You only need the sun.

The sun rises in the EAST every morning.

The sun sets in the WEST every evening.

So in the morning, stand and face the rising sun. You are now facing east.

When you face east:

    north is on your LEFT
    south is on your RIGHT
    west is BEHIND you

Try it tomorrow morning. Then you will never be lost about which way is which.
sections.example:
A map of a village.

This village is not a real place. It is drawn to practise on.

                    N
                    |
         [school]   |
                    |
     W ------- [market] ------- E
                    |
                    |
         [river]    |
                    S

Now read it.

The school is NORTH of the market. It is above it on the map.

The river is SOUTH of the market. It is below it.

If you stand at the market and walk north, you reach the school.

If you stand at the school and want to reach the river, you walk south — straight past the market and on.

Notice that direction works both ways. The school is north of the market, so the market is south of the school.

sections.heading: What a map is
sections.body:
A map is a picture of a place seen from ABOVE, as a bird would see it.

That is why a house on a map looks like a small square, not like a house from the front.

Maps use symbols — small pictures that stand for real things. A blue line might mean a river. A small square might mean a building.

The KEY tells you what each symbol means. Always read the key first, or you will guess wrong.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.body:
Use the village map above.

1. Name the four main directions in order, starting from north.

2. In which direction does the sun rise?

3. Is the school north or south of the market?

4. You are at the river. In which direction do you walk to reach the market?

5. Face the rising sun. Which direction is behind you?

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
• The four main directions are north, east, south and west.
• On a map, north is at the top.
• The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
• Face east and north is on your left.
• A map shows a place from above, and the key explains its symbols.

questions.question: In which direction does the sun rise?
questions.explanation: The sun rises in the east every morning and sets in the west every evening. This is why you can find your directions with nothing but the sun: face the rising sun and you are facing east.

questions.question: On a map, which direction is at the top?
questions.explanation: North is drawn at the top of a map, south at the bottom, east on the right and west on the left. Knowing this lets you read any map the same way.

questions.question: You face the rising sun. Which direction is on your LEFT?
questions.explanation: Facing the rising sun means facing east. When you face east, north is on your left, south is on your right and west is behind you. Try it outside one morning and you will remember it for good.
